entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Anselm of Laon (c. 1033-1117), a French theologian and philosopher, played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval intellectual landscape. He founded a school of scholars in Laon, which attracted prominent figures from across Europe.




Anselm's magnum opus, *Cur Deus Homo* (Why God Became Man), is a seminal work in the development of Scholasticism. In this treatise, he presented a novel Christology that posited Jesus Christ as both fully human and fully divine.




Anselm's influence can be seen in the works of later thinkers, such as Thomas Aquinas, and his ideas continue to be studied by scholars today.




In conclusion, Anselm of Laon's groundbreaking theology and educational endeavors left an indelible mark on Western intellectual history.
